- Base `pension_evt_income_change` (in this policy's `base_policy_refs`, `overwrite: []`): "An income increase lowers the rate effective the last day of the month in which the change began, and the lower rate is paid from the following month". - The extended rule: "The redetermined rate takes effect on the first day of the month after the month in which the most recent change it reflects began", which gives **2026-11-01**.

The care-cost rule says "A care-cost rate adjustment recomputes the annual pension when the veteran reports recurring care costs ... one that rests on a report the veteran sent, is recorded as soon as it is computed". A second solution, the care-cost adjustment in place of or in addition to the redetermination together with a statement hand-over, is defensible. -> **SOURCE-POLICY RED**.

G3 does not move this world: the spouse figure `3aa1499d` is on file, so the base is 22838, which equals base. G6 does not move it: the latest care month ends 29 days after its report, so every reading is "ongoing".

### problem_chain

Walked from the root:
1. Root = annual rate redetermination. The customer says "What you want is for VA to figure out what your pension will be going forward with all of this and put it on your record today". The trigger "When a veteran asks VA to settle what his pension will be after one-time payments and new care costs" is met. Prerequisite sentences in the root rule:
   - (a) "The redetermined annual rate is fixed only after the countable income on the award has been brought up to the recurring income on file."
     - At opening the award carries 27120.00 (= SS 15960 + spouse 9840 + interest 1320, the reports of 2025-09-18 with no COLA, interest scaling or compensation treatment).
     - The recurring income as redetermined now is 28206.45 (below), so the state is **false**.
     - Resolver: the recurring-income policy (`update_countable_income_81bdd26c`).
   - (b) "A redetermined annual rate is not recorded until the net worth on the award counts every one-time VA payment deposited since the award was granted."
     - At opening `net_worth` = 155520.00 = 128400 assets + 27120 income. It counts neither release `fe86d49a` (2026-10-01) nor refund `9b3b9bae` (2026-10-06), both after `opened_date` 2025-12-19, so the state is **false**.
     - Resolver: the net-worth policy (`update_net_worth_02de4f94`).
2. Net-worth rule:
   - (c) "Net worth is not redetermined until the award carries the veteran's own declaration of the one-time VA payments deposited to him, dated on the date of the most recent compensation release."
     - There is no `income_source=other` row at opening, so the state is **false**.
     - Resolver: the declaration policy (`declare_lump_sum_cb649dee`, owner=user).
   - (d) "Net worth is redetermined only after the countable income on the award reflects the recurring income on file as of the redetermination." This is false, as in (a); same resolver.
3. The declaration and recurring rules have no prerequisite.

Derived tree:
- root <- recurring (value_input)
- root <- net_worth (state_gate)
- net_worth <- declaration (value_input)
- net_worth <- recurring (value_input)

There are n = 3 prerequisite problems and 3 value_input edges, which is at least 2. No cycle. Topological order: {declaration, recurring} -> net_worth -> root. One problem (the declaration) is the customer's own write. The tree is isomorphic to the declared fields. The root also reads the declaration directly (`one_time_counted`, and "names as its source the veteran's one-time payment declaration") without an edge of its own; the order is entailed through (b)/(c) (`_difficulty.md` G19).

Load-bearing runs (my recompute with the charter's compute):
- Skip the declaration: net worth = **147061.67** instead of 159262.99. Bears weight.
- Skip the recurring write: net worth = **158176.54**, and the root (with net worth kept) = **18213** instead of 17126. Both edges bear weight.
- **Skip the net-worth write**: the root reads `net_worth` = 155520.00. That is at or below the limit 163699, so the rate is payable and the root = **17126**, unchanged. The redetermined 159262.99 is also at or below the limit. The state_gate edge root <- net_worth moves neither the root's scored value nor its terminal row. -> **SOURCE-CHAIN RED** (a decorative edge). The value_input floor is still met without it, but the edge exists only as ordering.

Parallel edges: declaration and recurring both feed net worth, and neither reads the other's output (the recurring compute reads no `income_source=other` row; the declaration reads no award figure), so either order gives the same terminal state. No wait. The tools judge nothing (`task_tools.py` lines 158-170, 190-192, 212-214, 246-257: create or update only).

user_scenario:

### task_independent_derivation

Identity: phone 9195550133 -> `1e6f619f...`. Verification takes three items (ssn 2731, file 320558417, DOB 1949-04-22). The award `04475a00` is Aid and Attendance, One Dependent, `running`. Act now.

**Declaration (owner user; agent computes, customer files).**
- `change_effective_date` = date of the most recent compensation release = **2026-10-01** (`fe86d49a`.payment_date).
- Period: the pension took effect 2025-11-01, 11 whole months before 2026-10-07 (fewer than 12), so only payments deposited in the whole months since the pension effective date are declared.
  - The overcollection refund `ece00c83` (2025-10-15) predates 2025-11-01 and is excluded. This is the near-miss.
- Release gross 15251.64, fee withheld 3050.32, debt withheld 2140.00 (`fe86d49a`).
- Fee: the comp award `2af02c64` has `attorney_fee_agreement_on_file` = true. The cap is 20% of 15251.64 = 3050.328, rounded to 3050.33. The fee 3050.32 does not exceed it, so the whole fee is taken out.
- Withheld part: no overcollection refund was deposited since the release (counting October 2026), so the whole 2140.00 is added back.
- Refunds: funding-fee refund `9b3b9bae` 492.00 was deposited in the period. The comp effective date 2023-06-01 is on or before loan closing 2024-04-15, so it is left out. No overcollection refund falls in the period.
- Release counted = 15251.64 - 2140.00 - 3050.32 + 2140.00 = 12201.32. Declaration = 12201.32 + 492.00 + 0 - 492.00 = **12201.32**.

**Recurring countable income (agent).**
- SS 15960.00, level 2024-12-01, 22 whole months: x1.028 = **16406.88**.
- Spouse 9840.00, level 2023-12-01, 34 whole months: x1.0537 = 10368.408, rounded to **10368.41**.
- Interest 1320.00, reported 2025-09-18. Assets on award = 155520 - 27120 = 128400.
  - Deposits since then: release net 10061.32 + funding-fee refund 492.00 + overcollection refund 260.00 (2025-10-15 is after 2025-09-18) = 10813.32. No transfers.
  - Scaled: 1320 x 139213.32 / 128400 = 1431.164, rounded to **1431.16**.
- Compensation: the award ended by election of pension, so **0**.
- Total **28206.45**.

**Net worth (agent), after both.**
- Assets last determined = 155520 - (15960 + 9840 + 1320) = 128400.00.
- Release since grant 2025-12-19: part withheld, so the net **10061.32** is added.
- Refunds since grant: funding-fee refund 492.00 plus overcollection refunds in that span (none; `ece00c83` predates the grant, the near-miss) = **492.00**.
- VA loan `b9f912bc`: active, `occupancy_certified` true, `partial_claim_balance` 0, so **0** is subtracted.
- Declaration received today (fresh), so it adds 12201.32 in full. Income = 28206.45 + 12201.32 = 40407.77.
- Medical deduction: medical reports are on file. 21240.00 - 1141.90 (threshold base 22838 because the spouse figure is on file) = 20098.10. That is positive and below the income, so the income counted is 20309.67.
- Net worth = 128400 + 10061.32 + 492 - 0 + 20309.67 = **159262.99**.

**Root — annual rate redetermination (agent), after net worth.**
- Countable income = 28206.45 + 12201.32 (fresh declaration) = 40407.77. Threshold 1141.90.
- Premiums: there are no medical-expense reports received 3-11 whole months ago. `0bb18750` (received 2025-09-18) is exactly **12 whole months** old.
  - Compute's half-open window puts it in "twelve to twenty-four whole months", giving Part B 202.90 x 12 x 2 (the category covers a spouse) = **4869.60**.
  - The rule's "between three and twelve whole months" also covers it, giving its total **4440.00** (G5).
- Care: four reports received 2026-10-02, total 5810, average 1452.50. The latest month (October, 1610) is above the average, so the monthly figure is 1610. October ends 29 days after the report, so the care is ongoing: x12 = **19320.00**.
- Deduction = 4869.60 + 19320 - 1141.90 = 23047.70. Income after = 17360.07. Net worth 159262.99 is at or below 163699, so the rate is payable.
- Annual = 34487 - 17360.07 = 17126.93, rounded down to **17126**.
  - Second reading (premiums 4440): deduction 22618.10, income after 17789.67, annual **16697**.
- `change_effective_date` **2026-11-01** under the extended rule (2026-10-31 under base, G2).
- `source_report_id` = the declaration's reference, returned by the user tool. `report_channel` = **phone**.
- Opening-world contrast for the root (before any prerequisite): 29328, computed with no declaration, award income 27120 and net worth 155520.

Write sequence: `verify_identity` -> `declare_lump_sum_cb649dee` (user, 2026-10-01, 12201.32) and `update_countable_income_81bdd26c` (28206.45), in either order -> `update_net_worth_02de4f94` (159262.99) -> `record_annual_rate_redetermination_a1a40d3e` (17126, 2026-11-01, declaration id, phone).

## findings

1. **SOURCE-POLICY RED — undeclared override of the decrease effective date.**
   - Root cause: `_difficulty.md` G2.
   - Evidence: base "An income increase lowers the rate effective the last day of the month in which the change began" against extended "takes effect on the first day of the month after the month in which the most recent change it reflects began"; `pension_evt_income_change` is in `base_policy_refs`, and `overwrite: []`.
   - Demonstrated consequence: `change_effective_date` 2026-10-31 (base, and real VA practice under 38 CFR 3.660(a)(2)) against GT 2026-11-01. The rate falls from 2288/mo to 1427/mo.
   - Affected: `pension_ext_annual_rate_redetermination` (overwrite/rule); GT step 20 argument.
2. **SOURCE-POLICY RED — the care-cost and annual-rate policies both claim this world's rate adjustment.**
   - Root cause: `_difficulty.md` G4.
   - Evidence: four veteran-sent care reports received 2026-10-02 (online); the care-cost rule "recomputes the annual pension when the veteran reports recurring care costs ... recorded as soon as it is computed"; and the customer's request for a settlement going forward.
   - Demonstrated consequence: the second solution records `record_rate_adjustment_fee79930` (2026-08-01, `d4b4bf2a`, online), preceded by a benefit-income-statement hand-over, rather than or besides GT step 20.
   - Affected: `pension_ext_care_cost_rate_adjustment` / `pension_ext_annual_rate_redetermination` triggers; GT steps 19-20.
3. **SOURCE-TASK RED — premium tier overlap gives a second root value.**
   - Root cause: `_difficulty.md` G5. "between three and twelve whole months" vs "twelve to twenty-four whole months".
   - Evidence: `pension_income_reports` `0bb18750` received 2025-09-18 is exactly 12 whole months before 2026-10-07.
   - Demonstrated consequence: premiums 4440.00 gives `adjusted_annual_rate` **16697**, against GT 17126.
   - Affected: `pension_ext_annual_rate_redetermination` rule (premium sentence), `computations[3]`, GT step 20.
4. **SOURCE-CHAIN RED — the state_gate edge root <- net worth does not bear weight.**
   - Evidence: payability `F('net_worth') <= 163699` holds at the opening (155520.00) and after the write (159262.99).
   - Demonstrated consequence: skipping `update_net_worth` leaves the root at 17126. The GT's own deletion run reports only the net_worth field itself.
   - Affected: `pension_ext_annual_rate_redetermination.prerequisite[1]`; the seed's net worth margins.
5. **SOURCE-FACTOR RED — four computations fall below the factor bounds once unreal ladders are struck.**
   - Root cause: `_difficulty.md` G5, G6, G7, G8.
   - Struck factors:
     - declaration: `debt_withholding_added_back` (one rule written as two) and `own_money_refunds_left_out` (unreal conditions; also read off the stamp `9b3b9bae.refund_basis = retroactive_compensation_award`, which names its tier-1 condition).
     - recurring: `interest_follows_savings` (one formula written as three tiers).
     - net worth: `compensation_release_cash` and `refunds_cash` (one rule written as several tiers) and the threshold-household ladder.
     - root: the threshold-household ladder, `premium_report_age` (G5) and `redetermined_care_months` (G6).
   - Demonstrated consequence (surviving factors): declaration 2 (1 parameter), recurring 3, net worth 3 (1 parameter), root 2 (0 parameter), each below 4 / 2 parameter.
   - Affected: the factors of the four task-1 policies; `computations[0..3]`.
6. Observations:
   - `_difficulty.md` G6: the care-months rule direction ("after the report reached VA") contradicts compute. There is no consequence here, because October ends after its report.
   - G19: the root reads the declaration without its own sentence.
   - The rule's "the fresh period" and "the ongoing-care gap" carry no day count in the prose (G15).
